analysis: This batch is documentation only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/installer-requires-macos27.md, lines 1-3) and a 5-line addition to docs/operations/provider-release.md (head lines 295-298). Both describe an installer behavior: scripts/install.sh `require_supported_macos` refuses a NEW install on macOS 26 or earlier before downloading the bundle, while an existing CLI or provider config can still reinstall or repair, with a notice to upgrade. The installer change itself is not in the supplied files, so I could not verify it. I examined the content against the threat model (TB-011, TB-002, T-052..T-057, A-016, A-017) and found no changed security control. The text does not alter attestation, authorization, App Attest proof lifetimes, build qualification, coordinator routing, key custody or encryption. Nothing here grants serving permission; the macOS gate only restricts onboarding of new providers. It is consistent with TB-011's note that macOS27+ onboarding waits for App Attest. The existing-install exemption leaves older-macOS providers on the legacy MDM/APNs path, but that path is unchanged and still governed by its own gates. The docs claim the installer 'refuses' on macOS ≤26 and exempts existing installs; the exemption's detection (CLI or provider config presence) is a local, user-controlled signal. That is only an onboarding UX gate, not a security boundary, since the operator controls the machine (ADV-001) and the coordinator enforces trust server-side. Remaining integration question for the next reviewer: when scripts/install.sh is reviewed, confirm that the version check fails closed on parse failure, runs before any download or execution, and does not weaken signature or hash verification in the repair path. Also confirm the doc claim 'refuses before downloading' matches the code.
